How a record enters

Benefit created or restored
The system produced an advantageous real-world change that was not principally the prevention of a specified imminent harm: an identifiable system, a real deployment, an identifiable beneficiary, an observed outcome.
Specific harm prevented
A dangerous pathway was operating, the system's intervention occurred, and the evidence supports that the intervention changed what happened.
Protective response, prevention unproven
The safeguard did something observable and appropriate, but no defensible counterfactual shows that harm would otherwise have occurred.
General benefit without an event
Launches, simulations, accuracy studies, aggregate claims, cohorts without an individually attributable changed outcome. Kept in the evidence base, off the depth scale.

Method

Admission

A record is admitted when a source reports that an AI system produced a beneficial impact. Nothing is discarded for weak evidence; the strength of the evidence is recorded as confidence and can be filtered on. Whether the benefit was what the system was built to do is recorded on every record and is not a condition of entry.

Kinds of event

A record describes one of four kinds of event. A benefit created or restored: an advantageous real-world change, with an identifiable system, a real deployment, an identifiable beneficiary and an observed outcome. A specific harm prevented: a dangerous pathway was operating, the intervention occurred, and the evidence supports that it changed what happened. A protective response whose prevention is unproven: the safeguard acted, but no defensible counterfactual shows that harm would otherwise have occurred. A general benefit without an event: launches, simulations, accuracy studies, aggregate claims and cohorts without an individually attributable changed outcome; these are kept in the evidence base and are not placed on the depth scale.

Depth

Each stakeholder group that benefited is rated from 1 to 5, the depth of the benefit for that group: 1, a convenience, or time or cost saved, with life otherwise unchanged; 2, a measurable improvement in a result or a capability, such as a test score or a crop yield; 3, a lasting change, a capability restored or a risk removed; 4, a serious harm averted or a serious condition resolved in time; 5, a life or a livelihood preserved, or a change documented across a population. Every rating carries its reason in full, so that a reader can see the judgment and not only the number. A group may be left unrated. Every rating is checked against its sources in a verification sweep, and any correction is recorded in the record's revisions.

The system's part

What the system contributed to the benefit is assessed separately from whether the benefit occurred, and may be left unrated. A system that was present is not thereby responsible.

Evidence and confidence

Every record cites its sources, each marked with its kind and with who wrote it: the system's makers, its deployer, the beneficiary, or someone independent of all three. Confidence is computed from them: high when an independent peer-reviewed study, case report, regulatory or court document or report supports the record; medium when the independent material is a news report, preprint or dataset, or when the makers', deployer's or beneficiary's own account is a peer-reviewed study, case report or official report; low when the only sources are press releases, announcements or other material from the makers, the deployer or the beneficiary. A registry label is one source among others.

Each record also states who stands behind its claim, from the strongest source on file: a court or a regulator, an independent study, independent reporting, or the beneficiary's, the deployer's or the makers' own account. Under its sources it says what is on file by kind and author, and what is not: an independent source, an independent study or report, a finding by a regulator or court. An unknown stays unknown; no field is filled by inference.

Briefs

Some records carry a brief from Peter H. Vartanian that distils the evidence and names its gaps, so that a reader deciding whether to act on a case can see what is established and what is not. The date of each brief is in the record's revisions.

Replication

Every record states which conditions produced the benefit and which of them would have to hold again. Attempts to make the benefit happen again are recorded with their setting, model version, and outcome, and drawn on the record's line of time. An outcome that nobody followed up is shown as unknown.

Harm on record

Where an incident database holds an entry about the same kind of system harming the same kind of stakeholder, the record links to it, so that a reader weighing benefit against risk can open both. No severity is shown for the harm.

Tools

The filters are tools. Each reader keeps the ones that the task needs and switches the others off; the choice is kept in the address, so that a view can be shared.

Not admitted

Candidates left out are duplicates of a record, events in which no AI system took part, topics with no case to record, and harms. Each is listed on the Not admitted (below) page with the reason, and the verifiers' full outputs are kept in the repository under data/review. Weak evidence does not keep a candidate out; it lowers the record's confidence.

Coverage

Counts on this site describe the database's coverage. They do not measure how beneficial AI is, and a trend in records is a trend in reporting.

Not admitted

Candidates examined and left out, with the reason. Weak evidence does not keep a candidate out; it lowers the record's confidence. What is left out is duplicates of records, events in which no AI system took part, topics with no case to record, and harms. The verifiers' full outputs are kept in the repository under data/review, and a candidate can be re-examined when better evidence appears.

Duplicate of a record

8
  • Face2Gene, consumer wearables, speech neuroprostheses and the brain-spine interface AIBD-0037

    These systems were not searched again because they are already in the database: Face2Gene (AIBD-0037), Apple Watch and other wearables (AIBD-0021 to AIBD-0027), speech neuroprostheses (AIBD-0002 to AIBD-0005) and the brain-spine interface (AIBD-0001). A new entry would repeat those records.

  • OECD AI Monitor entry on Casey Harrell's UC Davis speech neuroprosthesis AIBD-0002

    OECD AI Monitor entry 2026-06-15-4dfc covers the June 2026 press wave (Washington Post, 15 June; MIT Technology Review, 16 June) on Casey Harrell's UC Davis BrainGate2 speech neuroprosthesis, which is AIBD-0002, a record that already cites the NEJM 2024 paper and the Nature Medicine 2026 long-term-use paper.

  • OECD AI Monitor entry on Meta's self-harm alert and Meerut police in eight minutes AIBD-0010

    OECD AI Monitor entry 2026-06-08-7d81 (PTI via Rediff, ETV Bharat, The Hans India, LatestLY) describes the same event as AIBD-0010: Meta's alert to the UP Police Social Media Center at 6:53 pm on 7 June 2026 and Sardhana police at the 25-year-old's home within eight minutes.

  • OECD AI Monitor entry on Mia flagging Barbara's 6 mm cancer at NHS Grampian AIBD-0062

    OECD AI Monitor entry 2024-03-21-b742 (BBC, 21 March 2024; University of Aberdeen release) describes the same event as AIBD-0062, Mia flagging a 6 mm cancer missed by NHS Grampian radiologists in the GEMINI evaluation., 2026) and the 10 March 2026 Aberdeen release added to its evidence.

  • OECD AI Monitor entry on TrailGuard AI and the 39 poachers arrested in Similipal AIBD-0102

    OECD AI Monitor entry 2026-02-20-fae6 (The New Indian Express, Times of India and PTI, 20-21 February 2026) describes the same arrests as AIBD-0102; the agencies date the poachers' entry to Thursday night, 19 February, while the Field Director's account gives Wednesday night, 18 February.

  • OECD AI Monitor entries on Indian Railways AI elephant detection AIBD-0009

    Ten OECD AI Monitor entries on Indian Railways AI elephant detection (2023-03-20-b689, 2023-09-06-e510, 2023-11-29-0b17, 2024-02-09-5346, 2024-05-19-fc78, 2024-05-21-7e42, 2024-11-19-5a0a, 2025-08-12-50bf, 2025-12-20-724f, 2026-02-17-dcc6) repeat the Assam intrusion-detection case, AIBD-0009, and the Madukkarai thermal-camera case, AIBD-0101.

  • OECD AI Monitor entry on Tesla Autopilot avoiding a wrong-way driver AIBD-0109

    OECD AI Monitor entry 2020-03-07-752c, 'Tesla Autopilot Prevents and Fails to Prevent Collisions: Contrasting Incidents', corresponds to the Tesla Model S wrong-way-driver case in Cabarrus County already recorded as AIBD-0109.

  • OECD AI Monitor entry on Tesla Autopilot braking as an oak fell in Storm Dennis AIBD-0108

    OECD AI Monitor entry 2020-02-18-956e, 'Tesla Autopilot Prevents Fatalities During Storm Dennis by Emergency Braking', is the Tesla Model X oak-tree case already recorded as AIBD-0108.

No AI system took part

8
  • Spelling by a completely locked-in ALS patient (Chaudhary et al. 2022)

    The Nature Communications paper states that a multichannel decoding algorithm was not implemented: letters were selected by firing-rate thresholds with auditory neurofeedback, and the only support-vector machine belonged to an earlier eye-tracking system. No machine-learning system produced the benefit.

  • ChatGPT as manuscript editor for a missed-pneumothorax case report (Brown 2023)

    ChatGPT was used only to draft and edit the Cureus paper about a delayed pneumothorax diagnosis at Jersey General Hospital, and the paper's AI content is a proposal of how AI could have helped. No AI system took part in the patient's care.

  • BirdCast and the lights-out schemes of Raleigh and Bird Safe Philly

    Raleigh's Lights Out (27 August 2026) follows a fixed seasonal schedule from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m., with BirdCast mentioned only as a public resource, and Bird Safe Philly's page neither mentions BirdCast alerts nor reports collision results, so no AI output changed either decision. The BirdCast-driven case, Houston's Lights Out Nights, is AIBD-0103.

  • Titian catheter-robot ablation at Shaoxing People's Hospital (OECD AI Monitor entry)

    The only event in OECD AI Monitor entry 2025-12-13-c088, the Titian robot ablation on a 64-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation at Shaoxing People's Hospital (Xinhua Zhejiang, 13 December 2025), used a teleoperated master-slave catheter robot steered by the surgeon at a console, and the article never mentions AI, autonomy or inference. The entry's CA-GPT item is a 96-patient comparative preprint rather than an event, and its third source concerns an unrelated neurosurgical robot in Fushun.

  • Wandercraft Atalante exoskeleton walking for people with complete paraplegia

    Independent studies exist, including the 2026 Journal of NeuroEngineering and Rehabilitation trial of 11 participants at Nimes University Hospital, but the exoskeleton walks on trajectories precomputed by nonlinear optimization and tracked by a hybrid zero dynamics controller, with no machine learning or AI involved.

  • Estonia's small-claims 'robot judge'

    The Estonian Ministry of Justice stated on 16 February 2022 that it does not develop an AI robot judge for small-claims or general court proceedings to replace the human judge, so there is no system and no outcome to verify.

  • Rajesh Dandotiya bank-fraud intervention

    The intervention in the Rajesh Dandotiya case was made by human bank staff rather than by an AI system, so there is nothing to record.

  • Singapore Police Force Project A.S.T.R.O. scam alerts

    The Singapore Police Force's own description (MHA Minister's Awards page, 29 October 2024) says Project ASTRO uses robotic process automation to send SMS alerts to scam victims, and the Straits Times (16 April 2023) describes officers and OCBC staff analyzing fund flows and mass-sending SMSes with it. The S$442 million said to have been averted since April 2023 is a police aggregate for automated messaging, not for model-based detection.

Nothing to write up

14
  • AI embryo selection or AI newborn screening changing an identifiable patient's care

    No peer-reviewed case report of AI embryo selection or AI newborn screening changing an identifiable patient's care was found, so there was no system or case to examine.

  • An individual patient helped by a sepsis early-warning alert

    No individually documented sepsis early-warning case was found in a source independent of the developer; searches returned only cohort studies and implementation stories. The TREWS cohort evidence is recorded as AIBD-0066.

  • ChatGPT run after the fact on a necrotizing otitis externa case (Pugliese 2023)

    ChatGPT-3 and ChatGPT-4 were run on the Milan case only after the diagnosis had been made, did not suggest the correct diagnosis and had no part in the patient's care. The result is a failed test of the model, so there is no benefit to record.

  • A Garmin watch alert leading to a diagnosis

    No peer-reviewed case report of a Garmin alert leading to a diagnosis was found: Bogár et al. 2024 searched for Garmin and found none, and Europe PMC case-report searches returned no qualifying case.

  • A WHOOP alert leading to a benefit

    No peer-reviewed case report was found; only validation studies and vendor blog posts surfaced, with no case of a WHOOP alert leading to a benefit.

  • AI-detected fast radio bursts at CHIME in 2024

    Searches returned only machine-learning re-classification studies of the CHIME/FRB catalogs, not an AI-detected burst at CHIME in 2024 with independent confirmation, so there is no system or event to record. The Berkeley neural-network detection of FRB 121102 pulses is AIBD-0018.

  • An AI painting attribution accepted by a museum

    No museum statement accepting an AI-based attribution was located, and the candidate named no system, painting or museum; its other half, Ithaca, is AIBD-0017. The one named attribution case, Bradford's de Brécy Tondo, was examined under another theme and is AIBD-0276.

  • AI identification of the language of the Voynich manuscript

    No peer-reviewed acceptance of any AI identification of the Voynich manuscript's language was found, and no system, source or case was examined.

  • Machine-learning attribution of a work to Bach

    No peer-reviewed, scholar-accepted machine-learning attribution of a Bach work was found, and no system, source or case was examined.

  • Sign-language recognition or translation deployed for deaf users

    No deployed sign-language recognition or translation system with an independently evaluated outcome for deaf users was found. The 2026 JMIR systematic review of such systems for deaf health-care communication reports that every included system was at the development and testing stage and that contacted authors confirmed none had been deployed or commercialized.

  • AI interception of a fraud or scam with a named victim's loss prevented

    Searches returned only aggregate industry and regulator statistics on authorized push payment fraud; no court or regulator record of a specific AI interception with a named victim was found, and the candidate named no system, victim or event. The AI fraud-interception cases now in the database, such as TIAA's (AIBD-0210), came from other candidates.

  • An individual automatic emergency braking intervention that prevented a crash

    No regulator, court or peer-reviewed record of an individual AEB intervention in which the crash did not occur was found, and the NTSB documents located (Uber Tempe 2018, Ford BlueCruise 2026) record failures or disabled braking. The aggregate IIHS study is AIBD-0008; the Tesla incidents recorded from press reports (AIBD-0108, AIBD-0109) came from other candidates.

  • UIC trial of AI trespass detection on railways

    No UIC document naming an AI detection system or a trial result could be located: uic.org's safety pages list the TreSP network, TRESPAD events and project names such as AI4SAFEBEHAVE without any result, and its trespass-and-suicide page returned a 404 error. Nothing identifiable remains beyond the ProRail deployment, recorded separately as AIBD-0309.

  • An evacuation or emergency decision taken on an AI flood or nowcast forecast

    No authority statement documenting an evacuation or emergency decision taken on an AI flood or nowcast forecast was retrievable, and the candidate named no system, place or event of its own; the cases it pointed to are already AIBD-0031 (Bihar flood alerts) and AIBD-0092 (Mali skill evaluation). Actions on AI forecasts recorded from other candidates include the Kogi anticipatory cash payments (AIBD-0095) and the Philippine Red Cross activation (AIBD-0098).

A harm, not a benefit

1
  • Netherlands SyRI welfare-fraud risk scoring

    SyRI is a documented harm, a system the Hague District Court invalidated in 2020, and was set aside as such rather than examined as a benefit.

Data

The dataset is one file, records.json, released under CC BY 4.0. Three flat tables are derived from it: records.csv, one row per record; ratings.csv, one row per stakeholder group rated; and echoes.csv, one row per attempt to make a benefit happen again. The schema describes every field. Each record is also available on its own page as JSON.

Counting

One system, one setting, one benefit is one record. A benefit reported in several sources is one record with several sources. A benefit that happened again elsewhere is an echo on the original record, not a new record.

Fields

id
A stable identifier.
title, summary, date_observed, account
What happened, in one line and in one paragraph, and when.
brief
A brief from Peter H. Vartanian: his reading of the evidence and its gaps, where one has been written, with its sidenotes in brief_notes.
headline, metric
A short title that adds no fact, and the key quantified outcome copied verbatim from the summary or account (null when the record states no number).
category
The kind of event: benefit created, harm prevented, protective response (prevention unproven), or general benefit (no attributable event; kept off the scale).
unexpected, purpose
Whether the benefit was what the system was built to do, and what it was built to do.
system, model_version, developer, deployer, location, domain, segment
The system, its version where known, who made and ran it, and where it was used.
benefit_type, taxonomy_note
The benefit type from the taxonomy, with a note where the fit is loose.
ratings
For each stakeholder group that benefited, a depth from 1 to 5 or null for unrated, and the reason.
ai_role
What the system contributed, assessed separately, or marked not assessed.
evidence, confidence
The sources, each with kind, citation, link, date, a short quote, and who wrote it (the makers, the deployer, the beneficiary, or someone independent of them); confidence (high, medium, low) is computed from them as the method page describes.
comparator
Better than what: the baseline the benefit is measured against (against), the figure without and with the AI (before, after), whether the source measured or assumed the difference (basis), and the passage that states it (quote, url). Null when no source states a comparison.
later
What happened after the first report: persisted, scaled, reversed, withdrawn, litigated or unknown, with the date, a note, and the passage that states it. Unknown means nothing later was found.
value
A money figure a source states for the benefit: the amount verbatim with its currency, what it is, who gains or pays, whether the source calls it an estimate, and the passage. Never a figure of ours.
claim_status, claim_basis
Who stands behind the claim, from the strongest source on file (found by a court or a regulator, independently studied, independently reported, or the beneficiary's, the deployer's or the makers' own account), and the basis: the sources on file by kind and author, and what is not on file. Both are computed from the evidence.
replication
The conditions that produced the benefit, the conditions that must hold again, and the echoes (replications): each attempt to repeat it, with setting, model version, and outcome.
paired_incident
Harm on record: an entry in an incident database about the same kind of system harming the same kind of stakeholder, with the database's name and a one-sentence basis for the link.
registry_ids
Identifiers of the same event in other registries.
revisions
Every change, with its date, source, and editor.
